This method will work with any string of words or character found anywhere in the title. However, it is case sensitive, if you want to hide spoiler and Spoiler, for example, you would have to include both. If anybody can think of a better way please let me know. Remember to add a url to a legitimate image.

/* Hide thumbnail of posts containing [spoiler */ 
img[alt*="[spoiler"] {
 width:0px; 
 height:0px; 
 padding: 34px;
 background-image: url("%image_url%");
 background-size: contain;
 background-repeat: no-repeat;
}

/* Hide thumbnail of posts containing [nsfw] */
img[alt~="[nsfw]"] { 
 width:0px; 
 height:0px; 
 padding: 34px;
 background-image: url("%image_url%");
 background-size: contain;
 background-repeat: no-repeat;
}

Thanks to Xestrix the plurality issue has been solved.

I'm going to expand on this a little bit real quick.

[alt*="[spoiler"] Takes advantage of the fact that Voat assigns an alt attribute to all post with thumbnail img elements. These alt attributes are given a string value which is the same as the title of the post. That allows us to select the element and check the title for specific strings simultaneously. In other words this is saying: "select element containing alt attribute containing the string [spoiler". After that is done, we simply use the content property to change the img element's url to point wherever we want. It now hides the original thumbnail and changes the background to your selected image.

The difference between ~= and *= is that ~= checks for words (strings with spaces on either side) and *= checks for just strings.

tl;dr: If what's in the quotation marks of [alt*=" "] is EXACTLY matched anywhere in the title it will replace the thumbnail.
[Tip] Hide spoilers, nsfw, or any other post's thumbnail based on keywords
